text:
The Sharks beat Vegas 4-1 on Friday, and Max Miller of Sharks Hockey Digest pointed out what made it more than a win: it was the first time San Jose had ever beaten the Golden Knights in regulation at SAP Center, where Vegas had been 16-0-3. Macklin Celebrini sealed it with an empty-netter, and the Michael Misa, Alexander Wennberg and Tyler Toffoli line had what Miller called a dominant night.

That is the fun side of a rebuild that is starting to look like a team. Celebrini, Will Smith and either Igor Chernyshov or rookie Ivar Stenberg give San Jose a first line that wins its minutes (60% of the expected goals or better). Stenberg, featured in NHL.com's Rookie Watch, is finding his place, and Misa's name keeps surfacing in reports about a possible trade for Detroit's Simon Edvinsson, which the Sharks have not confirmed.

The less fun side is the blue line. San Jose gets 44% of the expected goals, among the lowest in the league, and allows the most expected goals per hour in this group. Darnell Nurse and Michael Kesselring have been outscored 15-7, and Ryan Warsofsky has been adjusting without Jacob Trouba. The penalty kill gives up almost a full expected goal a game.

At 12-14-2, the Sharks are a bit ahead of what their chances earned, and our numbers give them a 7% chance at the playoffs. What we'd watch: whether management trades young talent for a defenseman now, or lets the kids grow into it.
